codet:
These cases use the rule that each index can be decremented at most once per query, so index `i` can be reduced by at most `cnt[i]`, the number of queries covering it. The answer is `true` exactly when `nums[i] <= cnt[i]` for every `i`. I checked each expected output by hand against that rule.

```json
[
  {"input": "[0]\n[[0, 0]]", "output": "true"},
  {"input": "[1]\n[[0, 0]]", "output": "true"},
  {"input": "[2]\n[[0, 0]]", "output": "false"},
  {"input": "[2, 2]\n[[0, 1], [0, 1]]", "output": "true"},
  {"input": "[2, 2]\n[[0, 1], [1, 1]]", "output": "false"},
  {"input": "[3, 0, 0, 1]\n[[0, 0], [0, 0], [0, 0], [3, 3]]", "output": "true"},
  {"input": "[1, 1, 1]\n[[0, 1], [1, 2]]", "output": "true"},
  {"input": "[5, 5, 5]\n[[0, 2], [0, 2], [1, 1]]", "output": "false"},
  {"input": "[0, 0, 0, 0]\n[[0, 3]]", "output": "true"},
  {"input": "[2, 1, 2, 2, 1]\n[[0, 4], [1, 3], [2, 2], [0, 1]]", "output": "true"}
]
```
